penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: SaaS account recovery / escalation concierge inherently requires a human to interact with Google/Microsoft support channels on the client's behalf — there is no API to automate escalation with Google Workspace support.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Intake triage and status updates require direct client communication; the locked-out user needs to share account details and coordinate credential verification synchronously.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Each case is unique — different account states, billing histories, lockout causes — requiring human judgement throughout the resolution process.

rationale: The pain is acute and real — being billed while locked out with no resolution path is genuinely distressing for an SMB owner — but the proposed concierge service is fundamentally a human-labor product. Resolving Google Workspace admin lockouts requires a human to call Google support, navigate verification steps, and coordinate with the client; there is no automation path. The buyer pool is also fragmented and hard to reach (they're not congregating on a single reachable channel), and they experience this pain once, creating no recurring revenue. Operational autonomy is near zero.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for the factory's automation model. The service would require Youval personally to handle each support case — calling Google, gathering credentials, navigating account verification — with no repeatable automated delivery. Even if Claude drafts scripts and communication templates, a human must execute every step. This is a consulting/concierge business, not an automated micro-service. Drop and do not pursue.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy (3, well below 7 floor) and buyer_clarity (5, below 6 floor). One-time incident nature means no recurring revenue even if a case is resolved. Not a scalable autonomous product.
